subject: math
explanation:
Why Were Powers Invented?
Imagine I ask you to write:
2×2×2×2×2×2×2×2
Not too difficult.
Now imagine:
2 multiplied by itself 100 times.
Writing this becomes annoying.
Mathematicians wanted a shorter way.
So they invented:
28
instead of
2×2×2×2×2×2×2×2
This shorter form is called a power or exponent.

What Does 2⁸ Mean?
28
means:
2×2×2×2×2×2×2×2
Here:
Base

 2
The number being multiplied repeatedly.

Exponent (Power)
8
Tells us how many times the base is multiplied by itself.

Another Example
53
means:
5×5×5
= 125

Important Terms
Base
The repeated number.
Example:
In
74
Base = 7

Exponent
Number written above.
Example:
In
74

 Exponent = 4

Power
The complete expression.
Example:
74
is called a power.

Why Is This Useful?
Instead of writing:
10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10
we write:
106
Much shorter.
Much cleaner.
Scientists, engineers, programmers and calculators use this every day.

Special Cases
Any Number Raised to Power 1
51 = 5
Exponent 1 changes nothing.

Any Non-Zero Number Raised to Power 0
50 = 1
1000 = 1

brainstorming.question: Why do we write powers at all?
brainstorming.answer:
Because numbers can become enormous.
Imagine:

 10100
Writing:
10 × 10 × 10 × 10 ...
100 times
would waste time and space.
Powers are mathematical shorthand.
Just like:
"kg" is shorter than "kilogram"
Powers are shorter than repeated multiplication.

brainstorming.question: Why is 2³ called "2 cubed"?
brainstorming.answer:
Ancient mathematicians noticed:
23 = 8
can represent the volume of a cube with side length 2.
That's why power 3 became known as:
"Cubed"
Similarly:
22

 represents area of a square.
So it became known as:
"Squared"

brainstorming.question: Why is any number raised to power 0 equal to 1?
brainstorming.answer:
Observe pattern:
24 = 16
23 = 8
22 = 4
21 = 2
Every time exponent decreases by 1,
value divides by 2.
So:
20 = 1
The pattern demands it.

misconceptions.wrong: Any number raised to power 0 equals 0.

realLifeConnections.title: Real Life Connection 1 — Computer Storage
realLifeConnections.description:
Computers work using powers of 2.
Examples:
•

2¹⁰ = 1024 bytes

•

2²⁰ = 1 MB (approximately)

•

2³⁰ = 1 GB (approximately)

Every phone and computer uses powers.

sections.heading: 5. MISCONCEPTIONS
sections.content:
Misconception 1
2³ = 2×3
Wrong
23 = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8

Misconception 2
5² = 10
Wrong
52 = 25

Misconception 3

 Bigger exponent means addition.
Wrong
Exponent means repeated multiplication.

Misconception 4
Power and multiplication are unrelated.
Wrong
Powers are simply repeated multiplication.

Misconception 5
Any number raised to power 0 equals 0.
Wrong
50 = 1
